title: 2009 HMMT February General Round 1 Problem 8
statement: Let \(a, b\), and \(c\) be the 3 roots of \(x^{3}-x+1=0\). Find \(\frac{1}{a+1}+\frac{1}{b+1}+\frac{1}{c+1}\).

solutions.text: We can substitute \(x=y-1\) to obtain a polynomial having roots \(a+1, b+1, c+1\), namely, \((y-1)^{3}-(y-1)+1=y^{3}-3 y^{2}+2 y+1\). The sum of the reciprocals of the roots of this polynomial is, by Viete's formulas, \(\frac{2}{-1}=-2\).
